key_insight: SoundnessBench shows that frontier LLMs often overrate weak research ideas, revealing an optimism bias that makes them unreliable as first-pass judges of methodological soundness.
engineering_relevance: For AI-assisted research workflows, this means LLMs should be used as aids to screening and critique, not as standalone gatekeepers for deciding which ideas deserve compute and development time.
method: Built SoundnessBench from 1,099 ML research proposals reconstructed from ICLR submissions.
Annotated proposals with reviewer soundness sub-scores and audited them against source papers.
Evaluated 12 frontier LLMs under standard and aggressive prompting, plus controls for contamination and surface cues.
evidence_signal: The benchmark uses 1,099 reconstructed proposals with reviewer soundness labels, and the evaluation across 12 frontier LLMs found systematic false positives under standard prompting.
watch_item: SoundnessBench targets recoverable proposal-stage soundness, so it should not be treated as a direct predictor of full-paper review outcomes.
paper_title: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
